subject: mathematics
question_text: Is the matrix with rows (0, 1, 4), (−1, 0, 7) and (−4, −7, 0) symmetric or skew symmetric?

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.34, chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 17. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards writing the transpose separately from the comparison that names the type, because the transpose is the only real work and a one-word answer shows none of it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you decide which of the two it is, and give the answer.

steps.label: Write the transpose
steps.margin_note: First mark. Turn rows into columns. Row 1 of A becomes column 1 of Aᵀ, and so on.
lines: Turn the rows into columns to get Aᵀ:

recall.must_convey: That the transpose is written by turning each row of A into the matching column.
accept: write the transpose by turning rows into columns
row one becomes column one and so on
A transpose has rows zero minus one minus four, one zero minus seven, four seven zero
rows ni columns ga rasi A transpose teeyali

steps.why: Both tests, Aᵀ = A and Aᵀ = −A, are read off the same transpose, so writing Aᵀ once answers the whole question. Guessing from the look of the matrix is not a method a marker can credit.
common_mistakes: Reversing the order of the rows instead of transposing.
Naming the type with no transpose written.
steps.memory_tip: Transpose means row 1 becomes column 1, row 2 becomes column 2, row 3 becomes column 3.

steps.label: Compare and name the type
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Aᵀ ≠ A because of the (1,2) entry, and Aᵀ = −A entry by entry. The diagonal 0, 0, 0 is the extra sign that it is skew.
lines: Aᵀ ≠ A: the (1,2) entry is −1 in Aᵀ but 1 in A.
So A is not symmetric. Now write −A:
Every entry of −A matches Aᵀ, and the

lines.text: ∴ A is a skew symmetric matrix.

recall.must_convey: That Aᵀ is not equal to A but is equal to −A, so the matrix is skew symmetric.
accept: A transpose is not A but it does equal minus A so it is skew symmetric
the one two entry is minus one in the transpose and one in A so it is not symmetric
minus A matches the transpose entry by entry so it is skew symmetric
A transpose equals minus A kabatti skew symmetric
the diagonal is all zeros which fits skew symmetric

steps.why: The two tests are answered one after the other, so the answer is a decision and not a guess. The all-zero diagonal is a quick confirmation, because a symmetric matrix may have any diagonal while a skew symmetric one must have zeros.
common_mistakes: Calling it symmetric because the numbers 1, 4 and 7 reappear.
Deciding from the zero diagonal alone, with no comparison.
Writing −A but comparing it with A instead of with Aᵀ.
steps.memory_tip: Mirrored entries equal means symmetric; mirrored entries opposite in sign means skew symmetric.
